objectives: Decode taught words beginning with bl by mapping every grapheme in order.
Blend /b/ and /l/ smoothly before the vowel and final consonants.
Distinguish bl-words by their rime, including -ob, -ip, -ot, -ack and -ock.
Self-correct by checking the complete word rather than guessing from its first letter.
concepts: The onset bl contains two audible phonemes, /b/ followed by /l/.
The rest of a word must also be decoded; the blend alone does not identify the word.
Rimes help compare words but do not replace full grapheme-by-grapheme decoding.
Self-correction means returning to the graphemes when the spoken word does not make sense.

definitions.definition: Use grapheme-to-phoneme knowledge to read a written word.
The initial consonant sound or consonant group before the vowel in a syllable.
The vowel and following sounds in a syllable, such as -ob in blob.
Notice a mismatch and reread the word accurately.

workedExamples.solution: Map b-l-o-b to /b/ /l/ /o/ /b/, then blend: blob.
Keep bl together as two sounds, map a, then ck for final /k/: black.
Both begin with bl; the vowel and final consonant differ, so the words differ.

workedExamples.prompt: Correct a reading of block as bock.
workedExamples.solution: Return to the print, say /l/ after /b/, then blend block.

commonMistakes: Skipping /l/ and reading block as bock.
Guessing from the onset without decoding the rime.
keyTakeaways: Read bl as /b/ followed by /l/ without an extra vowel.
Decode the vowel and ending as carefully as the onset.
Compare rimes to notice differences among bl-words.
Reread and self-correct when the word does not match the print.
revisionPoints: blob has the rime -ob; blip has -ip.
blot has -ot; black has -ack; block has -ock.
Check every grapheme and reread the whole word.

basic.prompt: Which word ends in the rime -ip?

conceptual.prompt: Why must you read beyond bl?
conceptual.answer: The vowel and ending distinguish words such as blob and blip.

conceptual.prompt: What is the rime in blot?
What should you do if block is read as bock?
conceptual.answer: Return to the print and include /l/.

application.prompt: Read the onset and rime in block.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How do blob and block differ after the onset?
higherOrderThinking.answer: They have different vowels and endings: -ob and -ock.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Which word could fit a picture of a dark square toy: black or blip?
higherOrderThinking.answer: black, if the picture and context show the colour black.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why is sounding out safer than guessing from the first two letters?
higherOrderThinking.answer: It checks every grapheme and avoids confusing words with the same onset.

activities.name: Map and blend a chain of bl-words.
steps: Point to each grapheme in order.
Say /b/ then /l/ closely, without an added vowel.
Blend through the vowel and final consonant.
Reread the whole word and confirm it matches the print.

activities.name: Sort bl-words by rime and decode each word.
steps: Read blob, blip, blot, black and block.
Say the onset and rime for each word.
Explain why the same onset does not make the words identical.

outcomes: Decode taught bl-words accurately from left to right.
Identify the rime in a taught bl-word.
Correct a missed consonant by checking the written word.
Read a new taught-pattern word without adding a vowel to the blend.

questions.question: Which word contains bl and the rime -ack?
When decoding block, which sound must not be skipped?

answerKeys.explanation: The sequence ends with /o/ /b/, so the word is blob.
Blip ends with the final phoneme /p/.
The onset is bl and the rime is -ack: black.
The initial consonant group is bl.
Bag begins with /b/ and has no /l/ after it.
The vowel is short /i/ and the final sound is /p/: blip.
Sob and blob share the -ob rime.
Smooth blending keeps the blend intact and uses every sound.
Blot has onset bl and rime -ot.
The /l/ is the second phoneme in the initial blend.
The sentence states that a black blob is on the block.
